items.title: Oil's long view darkens as Middle East war refuses to end
items.summary: But traders are now betting that oil prices will remain elevated through 2028, forcing a rethink of the global inflation outlook. Global benchmark Brent crude futures tell the story. The International Energy Agency projects global supply will rise to 108.3 million barrels per day (bpd) next year from 100.7 million bpd this year as Middle Eastern exports recover.

items.title: Detained Suu Kyi receives UK royal package: Myanmar govt
items.summary: YANGON: Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi received a package from Britain's King Charles III on Monday, authorities said, releasing the first pictures of the detained Nobel laureate in two months and describing her as a "special female prisoner." Home ministry officials met her on Monday to deliver a package of two books about soil, "one sealed envelope, and a sealed diplomatic communication sent by King Charles III of the United Kingdom to the special female detainee", Myanmar's presidential spokeswoman said on her Facebook page. Accompanying the statement were two images of Suu Kyi meeting two men with their backs to the camera.

items.title: AI isn't Asia's only game in town
items.summary: Technology accounts for six of Asia's 15 best-performing market sectors this year thus far. North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato) members, which account for 65 per cent of global defence expenditure, committed in June last year to raise their annual defence spending to five per cent of gross domestic product by 2035. Global defence spending represented only 2.4 per cent of global GDP last year.

items.title: Haze: Indonesia probes 98 forest fire cases involving links to neighbouring countries
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian police have confirmed foreign involvement, including from neighbouring countries, in 98 corporate cases linked to the forest and land fires gripping the country. National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto said the Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) was working to identify those responsible and establish the nature of their involvement. However, at an earlier press conference, he said foreign assistance would have to wait until the Indonesian government declared the fires a national disaster.

items.title: Meta apologises after suspending "No Kings" Instagram account
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Meta apologised for suspending the Instagram account of the "No Kings" protest movement over the weekend, attributing the shutdown to a sharp increase in activity that looked like automated bot traffic rather than human exchanges. The Instagram account used by organisers and attendees, however, was offline for more than an hour. This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline," he said.

items.title: EPF, KWAP, Aberdeen pare CTOS stakes as shares plunge 44pct
items.summary: KWAP's latest disposal involved 1.77 million shares on Oct 16, reducing its stake to 191.81 million shares, or 8.724 per cent. Its holdings have declined by about 10.99 million shares since Sept 25. EPF, meanwhile, disposed of 1.31 million shares on Oct 14, bringing its holdings to 449.10 million shares, or 20.43 per cent.

items.title: 17 arrested over ECRL, Telekom Malaysia cable thefts
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Police have arrested 17 men suspected of belonging to four gangs linked to robberies and cable theft involving the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project and Telekom Malaysia in Temerloh. Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron identified the gangs as Geng Ravi, Geng Kepala, Geng Dany and Geng Mista. Police seized a one-tonne Mitsubishi lorry and several cut metal pole sections.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine got no warning as Russian missiles rain in
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed. "Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskyy said on the Telegram app. Zelenskyy said that the United States had slowed some vital supplies for Ukraine, adding that the delays were at the US Defence Department level.

items.title: PM calls for curfews in France as govt grapples with unrest
items.summary: PARIS: France's prime minister called for partial curfews Monday as protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre in Paris and authorities scrambled to stem public discontent fuelling cost-of-living demonstrations that over the weekend spilled over into some of the worst street violence in recent years. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out imposing a state of emergency after the interior minister said the police "had lost control" during the weekend's unrest, which has flared six months before France elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron. With organisers calling for a new round of protests next Saturday, Lecornu called for regional authorities to impose "partial" curfews to protect businesses and people after hundreds of shops were damaged and looted.

items.title: No agreement to provide financial support to AirAsia, says government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to low-cost carrier AirAsia amid financial difficulties linked to the Middle East conflict, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. "To date, the government has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to AirAsia, whether in the form of guarantees, loans or injections of public funds. He was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam), who asked whether the government was considering providing financial support to the AirAsia Group.

items.title: Muda unveils 25 policy proposals ahead of GE16
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Muda has launched its Buku 555 campaign, outlining 25 basic policy proposals ahead of the next general election, with a focus on a fairer economy and transparent public spending. Its president, Amira Aisya Abdul Aziz, said the campaign covered five themes, with estimated costs and funding sources for each proposal. She said the document would evolve based on public feedback and guide the party's policy advocacy in Parliament, state assemblies and its next election manifesto.

items.title: Search for missing 74-year-old woman to expand in Kubang Pasu
items.summary: KUBANG PASU: The search for a 74-year-old woman who went missing after leaving her home in Taman Kodiang, Changlun, will continue with a larger team involving several agencies and villagers. Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Zone 1 chief Senior Fire Superintendent Ahmad Aminuddin Abdul Rahim said the department received a call about the missing woman at 2.25pm. Kubang Pasu district police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said police received a report on the disappearance that day from a 53-year-old man at the Kodiang police station.

items.title: Queen donates 500,000 face masks to Johor schoolchildren
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, today donated 500,000 face masks to the Johor state government for distribution to schoolchildren across the state. Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present at the ceremony, held at the Johor City Council Tower Auditorium Hall. Also present were Johor State Secretary Datuk Mohammed Ridha Abd Kadir, state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, Johor Deputy State Secretary Datuk Nasri Md Ali and Johor Education Department director Zulkurnain Abdul Rahman.

items.title: Selangor PWD to add lane at accident-prone Alam Budiman junction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) plans to add a lane at the traffic light junction in Alam Budiman, Shah Alam, following recurring accidents involving heavy vehicles, particularly lorries. The medium-term measure will involve building an additional lane about 300m long from the Shah Alam direction, as well as improving street lighting and traffic lights at the junction, he said. The department has previously introduced several safety measures at the location, including a temporary lane, road signs and improved lighting.

items.title: Haze: Indonesia puts offers from Malaysia, others to combat forest fires on hold [WATCH]
items.summary: JAKARTA: Foreign assistance, including from Malaysia, to help Indonesia combat widespread forest and land fires will have to wait as the republic has yet to declare the situation a national disaster. Acknowledging Malaysia's offer of assistance, he said help would be forthcoming if the situation were declared a national disaster. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reaffirmed Malaysia's readiness to assist Indonesia and said Malaysia had proposed an Asean-level cooperation mechanism to strengthen coordination, preparedness and collective action against transboundary haze.

items.title: 6 arrested after Indonesian woman rescued with burns
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Six men, including an employer, have been arrested after police rescued an Indonesian woman who was abused and left with burns across her body. Seberang Prai Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman said the operation was linked to a case reported in Tanjong Sepat, Selangor. The operation was carried out by the Selangor police contingent's Criminal Investigation Department, together with the Kuala Langat district police Criminal Investigation Division, with assistance from the Penang police forensic team.

items.title: TNB, PTP in strategic partnership to power Malaysia's net-zero aspiration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has entered into a strategic partnership with Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), a member of the MMC Group, to support Malaysia's decarbonisation agenda and enhance sustainability compliance via greater renewable energy (RE) adoption under the Green Electricity Tariff (GET) programme. "Under the partnership, PTP subscribed to 16,000 blocks of GET, equivalent to 16GWh of certified green energy per month, for the period from May 2026 to December 2027," the statement said. NEW BENCHMARK FOR SUSTAINABLE MARITIME OPERATIONS Through the GET programme, PTP will receive certificates that correspond to its green energy subscription.

items.title: Ex-delivery rider jailed 30 years for meth trafficking
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A former p-hailing delivery rider was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane by the Ayer Keroh High Court after being found guilty of trafficking 684g of methamphetamine five years ago. Judge Datuk DJP Suria Kumar sentenced Muhammad Nadhir Zailany, 31, after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt over the prosecution's case. The judge said the defence had questioned the prosecution's failure to call a man known as "Hafiz", whom the accused claimed was the actual owner of the drugs, as well as its failure to call Inspector Hasif as a witness.

items.title: Malaysian recounts harrowing walk through Paris protests
items.summary: Izdiharuddin was in Paris under the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to participate in Salon International de l'Alimentation (SIAL Paris 2026), an international food and beverage exhibition. [[nid:1559207]] Despite the unrest, he said he would proceed with his scheduled business meetings at the exhibition, adding that his daily journeys between the hotel and exhibition centre remained relatively safe. He said Malaysian delegates attending the food fair remained safe, with the unrest largely confined to central Paris.

items.title: IHH Healthcare Malaysia expands Gleneagles Hospital Johor with Afiniti Wellness acquisition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Pantai Medical Centre Sdn Bhd, has entered into an agreement to acquire Afiniti Wellness in Medini, Iskandar Puteri, Johor, laying the foundation for an integrated healthcare campus spanning approximately 18 acres. The move forms a key part of Gleneagles Hospital Johor's next phase in Medini. Dr Kamal Amzan, chief executive officer of IHH Healthcare Malaysia, said: "Johor is entering an important period of growth with establishment of the JS-SEZ, and Gleneagles Johor is ready to support the state's rising healthcare needs," said Dr Kamal Amzan, chief executive officer of IHH Healthcare Malaysia.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 19, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Anwar addresses debts The government must continue paying 1MDB debts, including interest, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Christy Ng defends suit Fashion entrepreneur Christy Ng says her defamation suit aims to protect the livelihoods of nearly 500 employees. PAC probes highway project The PAC will investigate management, finances and implementation of the Pan Borneo Highway Sabah Phase 1 project.

items.title: Kelantan folks say ECRL fares are reasonable
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The people in Kelantan have described the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) fares of RM125 to RM147 for journeys between Gombak and Kota Baru as reasonable, given the shorter travel time. I think fares of between RM125 and RM147 are reasonable. Kelantan People's Action Council president Aiman Yusri Mohd Yusoff also considered the fares reasonable, given the journey time and service provided.

items.title: CAB Cakaran teaming up with Oiltek in palm oil-based animal feed ingredients
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CAB Cakaran Corp Bhd is teaming up with Oiltek Global Pte Ltd to explore a joint venture to develop premium animal feed ingredients from palm oil-derived products. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, CAB Cakaran said the proposed collaboration combines its expertise in animal nutrition, feedmill operations and livestock production with Oiltek Global's palm oil processing technologies. Oiltek Global, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Singapore-listed Oiltek International Ltd, will contribute its proprietary technology, processing know-how and engineering capabilities.

items.title: KL20 startup investments generate RM202.64bil in sales proceeds since 2024
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Investments in startups since the launch of KL20 in 2024 have generated total sales proceeds of RM202.64 billion, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said investments channelled into the startup ecosystem amounted to about RM50 billion since 2024. On the government's target of producing five unicorn companies by 2030, Akmal Nasrullah said the government was still working to strengthen the startup ecosystem.

items.title: Propel Global proposes diversification into property development to revive earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Propel Global Bhd had proposed to diversify its core operations to include property development, entering a new sector as it seeks to rebuild profitability following two consecutive years of steep net losses. "The property development business is also complementary to the group's existing technical services segment, allowing the group to leverage its experience in engineering, construction and project management in undertaking property development projects. For FY25, revenue contracted to RM111.5 million, resulting in a net loss of RM24.2 million.

items.title: 3,000 Malaysians in France safe amid nationwide protests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All 3,000 Malaysians registered with the Malaysian embassy in France are safe and accounted for amid ongoing nationwide protests, says Malaysian Ambassador to France Datuk Eldeen Husaini Mohd Hashim. Eldeen said major cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Lille, had seen large demonstrations, with the number of protesters estimated at between 500,000 and 600,000. "As of today, we have around 3,000 Malaysians registered with us in France, including about 300 in Paris and the rest scattered all over.

items.title: Government mulls eKYC, age verification for online gaming platforms, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will examine the feasibility of extending electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) and age verification requirements to online gaming platforms such as Roblox. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move would take into account various aspects, including underage users and the possibility of the platforms being misused by extremist, radical and terrorist groups. Fahmi said the government, including through the National Security Council, continuously monitors platforms that could be misused by such groups.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt to study identity, age checks for Roblox and online gaming platforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The government will examine the feasibility of expanding the implementation of electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) verification and age verification to online gaming platforms such as Roblox, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the move will take into account various aspects, including issues involving underage users as well as the possibility of the platforms being abused by extremist, radical, and terrorist groups. The issue might only be in terms of user verification and user age verification.

items.title: MMAG disposes a freighter aircraft at RM12.7mil loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd, through its indirect unit MJets Air Sdn Bhd, is disposing of a Boeing B737-400SF converted freighter for US$2.8 million (RM11.43 million), as part of its ongoing review of its aviation assets and operations. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the group said MJets Air had entered into an aircraft purchase agreement with Mont Gabanon Airlines on Oct 19. The aircraft was acquired by MJets Air on Jan 24, 2025, for US$6.55 million.

items.title: UM student who questioned donations to Najib stands by remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya student Ummi Umairah Bakhit will not retract her remarks about public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which she made at a summit here recently. I hope more people will find the courage to speak up about corruption and integrity without fear," she said in a post on her Instagram account today. Ummi said her views remained unchanged and that she remained committed to the principles of integrity, equality and justice, as well as opposing corruption.

items.title: Malaysia, Japan explore defence technology transfer, local industry cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Malaysia and Japan have the potential to expand defence industry cooperation through technology transfer, local component development and participation in global supply chains, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “I received a briefing on Japan’s approach to developing its defence industry, while exchanging views on potential cooperation in technology transfer, local component development and global supply chains. “I believe closer ties based on trust and mutual respect will open up more opportunities for defence cooperation that benefit both countries,” he posted on X, explaining that ATLA was an agency under Japan’s Ministry of Defence responsible for defence procurement, technology and logistics.

items.title: Johor police arrest 13 over Molotov cocktail attack on Myanmar refugee homes in Kulai
items.summary: Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police nabbed the suspects, aged between 16 and 31, in Kulai district in an operation conducted from October 14 until yesterday. He said the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID), together with the Kulai District Police Headquarters (IPD) CID, carried out the arrests based on public information. Ab Rahaman said police remanded four suspects for eight days beginning October 14, four for a week, and one for five days beginning October 15, while remanding four others for a week starting today.

items.title: Budget 2027 debate: Calls for fairer MP allocations, faster migrant deportations and tax relief for caregivers
items.summary: Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) urged the government to enact legislation to ensure constituency allocations for MPs were distributed according to a proportional formula based on the number of voters and residents, regardless of political affiliation. Other constituencies, meanwhile, have only half or a third of Bangi’s number of voters. “Many people want to care for their parents at home and provide personal care.

items.title: Kelantan police arrest man over alleged indecent act involving cat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A man has been arrested in Kelantan to assist investigations into a viral video allegedly showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat at his home. Pasir Puteh district police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said police received a report on October 18 after the video circulated on social media platform Threads. He said police subsequently arrested a man to assist with further investigations, with the case being investigated under Section 377 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: ‘Justice has prevailed’: Teresa Kok wins RM250,000 defamation suit against Dr Akmal over halal certification row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Seputeh MP Teresa Kok has won RM250,000 in damages in her defamation suit against Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh over remarks he made during a dispute on halal certification. In a statement posted on Facebook, Kok said she hoped the judgment would serve as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly. “I hope this judgment serves as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly.

items.title: Selangor Sultan launches Silver Jubilee book, stamps and coins marking 25 years on throne
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today launched a commemorative book, first-day cover and stamps, and special coins in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign. Also present at the ceremony at Pustaka Raja Tun Uda here were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah. Accompanied by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Sultan Sharafuddin officiated at the launch of the commemorative items, presented as tokens of appreciation by the Selangor government in collaboration with the Selangor State Treasury, Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) and Pos Malaysia Bhd.

items.title: Proposed Kuching international airport could contribute RM1.8b annually to Sarawak GDP by 2050, says state minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 19 — The proposed New Kuching International Airport (NKIA) at Tanjung Embang could contribute approximately RM1.8 billion annually to Sarawak’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2050 under a high-growth scenario. “The study also projected that NKIA could support approximately 37,919 full-time equivalent jobs across the wider economy. During construction, Phase One could support around 9,393 jobs annually over the projected six-year construction period.

items.title: AGC to appeal against Session Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Papagomo of sedition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, of a sedition charge. In a statement today, the AGC said the decision was made after examining the ruling of the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court sitting in the Klang Sessions Court today, which acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, at the close of the defence case for a charge under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 (Act 15). “The accused presented his defence by giving sworn testimony in the same Sessions Court.

items.title: Semporna’s illegal foreign business activities raised in Cabinet, says minister
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Oct 19 — The issue of foreigners abusing social visit passes to engage in illegal economic activities in Semporna has been raised and discussed in the Federal Cabinet, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. “Action is being taken on this issue, with operations conducted particularly against business activities on the islands. “The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) has also discussed this issue and will take appropriate action,” he told reporters after an official working visit today to assess border control preparedness at Pulau Ligitan, Pulau Sipadan and Pulau Mabul.

items.title: Sabah registers 38,659 commercial vehicles under subsidised diesel scheme
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 19 — A total of 38,659 commercial vehicles belonging to 17,703 companies in Sabah have registered under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) as of yesterday, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali He said the registrations comprised 27,655 vehicles transporting essential goods, 8,773 company-owned vehicles, including jeeps and pick-up trucks, and 2,231 public land transport vehicles. Armizan said 1,408 vehicles belonging to 995 companies in Sabah had also registered under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS). These comprised 788 public land transport vehicles and 620 vehicles transporting essential goods.

items.title: Sarawak targets 15,000MW power capacity by 2035, with 60pc from renewables
items.summary: “The Baleh hydroelectric plant, with a capacity of 1,285 MW, is expected to operate in the fourth quarter of 2029. The Samalaju CCPP, with a capacity of 1,500 MW, is scheduled to operate in phases, with Blocks 1 and 2 having a total capacity of 1,000 MW expected to operate in the second quarter of 2027, while Block 3 with a capacity of 500 MW is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. “Currently, Sarawak exports an average of 100 MW to West Kalimantan and 30 MW to Sabah.

items.title: Malaysia retains WHO validation for eliminating mother-to-child HIV, syphilis transmission
items.summary: In a statement, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement reaffirmed the recognition first obtained in 2018, when Malaysia became the first country in the WHO Western Pacific Region to receive the validation. The ministry said the recognition reflected Malaysia’s continued commitment to strengthening maternal and child health and ensuring access to quality screening, treatment and healthcare services. According to the MOH, screening coverage for HIV and syphilis among pregnant women remained above 95 per cent throughout the assessment period, while antiretroviral treatment coverage among pregnant women living with HIV reached approximately 99 per cent.

items.title: Data Centre Bill to go to Cabinet in 2027, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy, in addition to addressing utility constraints and avoiding imbalances in environmental impact. He said the agreement was reached following the presentation of the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development by the Ministry of Digital. Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries, along with the implementing agencies, would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Ministry of Economy.

items.title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 shuttle buses for Malaysian GP at Sepang
items.summary: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service was aimed at meeting the transport needs of motorsports fans and facilitating their journeys to the circuit. He said tickets would go on sale from October 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub. Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from three main locations, namely the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.

items.title: Anwar congratulates para cyclist Zuhairie on winning Malaysia’s first gold at 2026 Asian Para Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi for winning Malaysia’s first gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. “Congratulations and well done, Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi. Zuhairie secured Malaysia’s first gold medal at the Games after winning the men’s C4-C5 (physical impairment) 1,000-metre (m) time trial final at the Izu Velodrome earlier today.

items.title: Haze: 27 areas in Malaysia record unhealthy air quality as of 4pm, Johan Setia in Selangor records highest reading of 169
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A total of 27 areas nationwide continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading of 169. Six areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tangkak (161), Pasir Gudang (157), Batu Pahat (156), Larkin (140), Kota Tinggi (128) and Kluang (105). A total of 38 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three areas - Labuan (48), Kimanis in Sabah (43) and Limbang in Sarawak (35) - recorded good readings.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Pahang to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: In Melaka, the State Education Department said that students attending school were encouraged to wear face masks, while parents or guardians who were concerned about their children’s health were allowed to keep them at home, provided that they informed the school. In Selangor, the State Education Department also said that schools would operate as usual, but outdoor activities had been postponed, with students attending school encouraged to wear face masks. In Negeri Sembilan, the State Education Department said that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) across the state would also operate as usual tomorrow.

items.title: MyEG probe into RM230.9m govt revenue case widens, 15 questioned, including 12 JPJ officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The police have recorded statements from 15 individuals to assist in investigations into allegations of failure to transfer RM230.9 million in government revenue, involving MyEG Sdn Bhd (MyEG) and Zetrix AI Berhad. Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said those questioned comprised 12 Road Transport Department (JPJ) officers and three bank officers. “So far, statements have been recorded from 15 individuals, comprising 12 from JPJ and three bank officers,” he said today.

items.title: Businessman loses appeal to claim RM185,671 lottery prize without ticket in Shah Alam court
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — A businessman has failed in his bid to recover RM185,671 from Pan Malaysian Pools Sdn Bhd after losing his winning lottery ticket. At the Shah Alam High Court today, judicial commissioner Seow Hock Peng dismissed M Mahendravarman’s appeal against a Sessions Court ruling that rejected his claim against the lottery operator, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. The company refused to pay without the original ticket.

items.title: Religious scholars must keep up with advances in science and technology, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Religious scholars need to broaden their knowledge by keeping abreast of developments in science, technology and geopolitics to ensure that the message of dakwah remains relevant in addressing contemporary global challenges. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said mastery of contemporary knowledge must go hand in hand with the study of traditional Islamic knowledge and ‘turath’ (Islamic classical heritage) to enable religious scholars to understand global changes and address the challenges facing the ummah more comprehensively. Zulkifli said global technological and geopolitical developments required society, including religious scholars, to understand strategic issues and avoid becoming preoccupied with trivial matters and differences of opinion that offered little benefit.

items.title: Poultry farm operator slapped with RM50,000 fine for fly breeding offence
items.summary: PARIT BUNTAR, Oct 19 — A poultry farm operator was fined RM50,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of allowing fly breeding at two poultry farm premises in Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, last July. According to the first charge, Siah was accused of allowing fly breeding at a PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm at Lot 5020, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 9.40 am on July 16. He was also charged with committing the same offence at another PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm along Jalan Changkat Lobak, Beriah, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 12.16 pm on the same day.

items.title: Lawyer says eviction bid halted, court order to be sought for Balai Undang Rembau
items.summary: REMBAU, Oct 19 — The Balai Undang Luak Rembau today faced another attempt at eviction when several senior government officials arrived to reclaim possession of the premises. Online . Lawyer representing the Balai Undang Luak Rembau, Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, said those present included the director of the Land and Mines Office (PTG), the Rembau district officer, the district police chief and several other department heads.

items.title: KL JPJ records RM376,091 in proceeds from seized vehicle auction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (JPJ) generated RM376,091 from its Public Auction of Seized Vehicles (Series 2/2026), conducted through the JPJvBID system. Its director, Hamidi Adam, said 120 of the 157 vehicles offered were successfully auctioned, surpassing the results of the previous auction series. Hamidi said the results reflected the effectiveness of the JPJvBID system as a transparent, efficient and accessible digital auction platform.

items.title: Traffic diversion on Butterworth-Kulim Expressway for two hours from 10.30am on Oct 21
items.summary: During the exercise, affected motorists will be diverted through the eastbound Penanti Rest and Service Area (R&R). The exercise aims to assess PLUS and the relevant agencies’ preparedness, response time and coordination in handling highway emergencies, as well as evaluate accident response and safety procedures. Participating agencies include PLUS, the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Health Ministry (KKM), Department of Environment (DOE), Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM), transport strategic partner Prifaria Sdn Bhd and highway maintenance contractor Edgenta Infrastructure Services (EIS).

items.title: Wan Saiful urges Putrajaya to consider shutting pig farms, says imported pork ‘safer’, may be cheaper
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — Opposition lawmaker Wan Saiful Wan Jan today urged the federal government to consider shutting down pig farms nationwide, as Putrajaya reviews the industry chain. “Personally, I feel it would not be excessive for me to propose that the federal government consider whether it is appropriate for Malaysia to continue having large pig farms when pork supplies can be obtained through imports, as done in Singapore. Wan Saiful added that pig farming in Malaysia was likely to face opposition from local residents regardless of location, describing Singapore’s reliance on imports as a “safer” approach.

items.title: Court of Appeal revives 1MDB bid to challenge US$3.7b judgment against Jho Low and father
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — The Court of Appeal today gave 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and four of its subsidiaries another chance to challenge a High Court ruling that ordered fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and his father, Larry Low Hock Peng, to pay more than US$3.7 billion. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the three member bench, chaired by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli, directed that the application be heard afresh before a different High Court judge. Neither Jho Low nor his father was present or represented in court.

items.title: PAC launches probe into Sabah Pan Borneo Highway after audit reveals delays despite RM10.5b spent
items.summary: PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said that from 2016 to March 31, 2026, RM10.547 billion, or 94.6 per cent of the RM11.153 billion allocation, had been spent, although the project’s physical progress was far behind schedule. She disclosed that the 706-kilometre (km) project, comprising 35 work packages, was expected to be fully completed by the end of 2021, but only four work packages, or 11.4 per cent, had been completed. “While the remaining 31 work packages, worth RM16.319 billion, are still being implemented, the project should have been completed five years ago.

items.title: On loan to Japan, welfare row over Dara, Amoi and Kelat flares up again as Taiping council holds off on latest claims
items.summary: Dara, Amoi and Kelat have lived at Tennoji Zoo in Osaka since March under a 25-year cooperation deal with Taiping Zoo & Night Safari. She said such behaviour calls for a professional assessment of the elephants’ psychological health, Berita Harian reported today. Her group has had two staff at Tennoji Zoo since April, recording the elephants’ behaviour daily.

items.title: Papagomo walks free after acquittal on sedition charge over Facebook remarks
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, was acquitted and discharged by the Klang Sessions Court today of a sedition charge over remarks allegedly made on Facebook three years ago. His lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said Judge Siti Aminah Ghazali delivered the decision at the conclusion of the defence case. He said only Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, testified for the defence, while Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Mustaffa P. Kunyalam prosecuted the case.
